newsitem.title: USA: Ultrak not looking for new merger partner.
newsitem.headline: Ultrak not looking for new merger partner.

text.p: Ultrak Inc President and Chief Executive Officer George Broady said the security products company would not be looking for new merger partners following the collapse of its merger plans with Checkpoint Systems Inc.
"We have not been, and we are not, looking for another merger partner," Broady said on a conference call.
He said Ultrak was not searching for a merger until it was approached by Checkpoint, and saw it as a very good fit. He said he was "disappointed" the deal had fallen through.

The two companies announced Thursday that Checkpoint's plans to acquire Ultrak were dropped by mutual consent because of perceived differences in sales methods. Broady said some of Checkpoint's clients were happy with its direct sales approach and did not want a third party brought in.
Under terms of the pact, each Ultrak share would have been exchanged for 1.15 Checkpoint shares. Wall Street arbitrage traders said then the deal was valued at about $397 million.
Also Thursday, Ultrak said its first quarter primary earnings from operation would be between $0.16 and $0.18 per share, lower than the First Call consensus of $0.21.
Ultrak's shares were trading 4-3/4 lower at 11-3/4 on the Nasdaq National Market before noon on Friday, after earlier dropping as low as 10-1/4.

Broady said he was extremely optimistic about Ultrak's growth prospects but noted that first quarter revenues of about $42 million were five percent lower than originally projected and said analysts would be well advised to set conservative revenue estimates for 1997.

"We were short about five percent in the first quarter. We had rising expectations of revenues built in to the plan before and I think it is a conservative approach to cut revenues estimates by five percent for the year -- that's roughly $10 million -- until we prove differently. I don't see any problem with that. The burden of proof is on us," Broady said.
